newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Ecopetrol '96 oil export revenues up.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ecopetrol '96 oil export revenues up.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol said in a statement on Tuesday its oil export revenues rose 23.5 percent to $1.11 billion in 1996.
The rise in the value of exports came against the backdrop of a fall in the volume of exports, down 1.08 percent to 53.4 million barrels in the year, the statement added.

Imports of gasoline fell 24 percent in volume to 8.8 million barrels in 1996 but rose 2.14 percent in dollar value, Ecopetrol said. The fall in the volume of gasoline imports has been largely due to an increase in refining capacity in the oil production center of Barrancabermeja.
No figures were available for the volume of oil exported by private sector companies which operate fields in association with Ecopetrol.
Last year, total Colombian oil production averaged 628,000 barrels per day and is scheduled to rise to 723,000 barrels per day in 1997.
Ecopetrol forecasts that oil output from the fields it operates on its own, without associated companies, will rise 13.7 percent to 473,000 barrels per day by mid-1997.
